topics.title: A Lakh Varieties and Getting a Feel of Large Numbers

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise one lakh as 1,00,000, the smallest 6-digit number, and compare quantities with it.
Get a sense of large measurements by comparing them with familiar quantities.

topics.title: Reading and Writing Numbers in the Indian System

concepts.learning_objective: Place commas in the Indian place value system and identify the place of each digit.
Convert between numerals and number names using lakhs and thousands.

topics.title: Land of Tens: Place Value through Button Clicks

concepts.learning_objective: Find how many presses of +10, +100 or +1000 buttons make a given number.
Explain why the fewest button clicks for a number equals the sum of its digits.

topics.title: Of Crores and Crores: Indian and American Systems

concepts.learning_objective: Relate thousand, lakh, crore and arab and count the zeroes in each.
Read, write and compare numbers in the Indian and American (International) systems.
Decide when rounding up or rounding down is appropriate in a real situation.
Find the nearest thousand, ten thousand, lakh, ten lakh and crore of a number.
Estimate sums and differences of large numbers and judge which estimate is closer.
Regroup factors such as 5 = 10/2 and 125 = 1000/8 to multiply quickly.
Predict the possible number of digits in a product from the digits of its factors.

topics.title: Did You Ever Wonder...? Thought Experiments

concepts.learning_objective: Make reasonable assumptions to test whether a large-number claim is possible.
Carry out large calculations in stages to answer distance and time questions.
